You are reviewing a small uncommitted Go diff in the repo at /Users/pfleidi/entire/cli/.entire/worktrees/pfleidi-cor-1430-cli-enable-async-mirror-creation-by-default (run all commands from there; do not cd elsewhere). Angle: ALTITUDE. Check that each change is implemented at the right depth rather than as a fragile bandaid. Special cases layered on shared infrastructure are a sign the fix isn't deep enough; prefer generalizing the underlying mechanism. Do not hunt for correctness bugs.

Context: the previous version of this branch made `AsyncMirrorRequests bool` default to true by passing a defaults struct into a `loadFromFileWithDefaults` helper used only by `loadMergedSettings`. That broke a requirement: a settings read-modify-write (LoadFromFile then Save) must preserve an explicit `"async_mirror_requests": false` and must not add the key when it was absent. The fix under review turns the field into `*bool` (nil = default true), adds `IsAsyncMirrorRequestsEnabled()`, switches the merge to `mergeRawBoolPtr`, deletes `loadFromFileWithDefaults`, and adds a save-roundtrip test.

Run `git diff HEAD` to see the diff (files: cmd/entire/cli/repo_mirror.go, cmd/entire/cli/settings/settings.go, cmd/entire/cli/settings/settings_test.go). Then check: (1) how the codebase already models "default true, explicitly settable to false" settings — look at `SignCheckpointCommits` / `IsSignCheckpointCommitsEnabled`, other `*bool` fields in EntireSettings, and `mergeRawBoolPtr` callers — and whether the new field follows that same mechanism or invents a parallel one; (2) whether every consumer of `AsyncMirrorRequests` now goes through the accessor (rg for `AsyncMirrorRequests` across cmd/ and e2e/), so the nil-default logic is not re-derived at call sites; (3) whether the `Enabled: true` default hardcoded in `loadFromFile` is the established pattern or whether the diff should have kept a defaults mechanism; (4) whether `Save`'s serialization path (look at Save and how it handles omitempty pointer fields) needs anything else for pointer bools, comparing with how SignCheckpointCommits is persisted.

Report findings as: file, line, one-line summary, concrete cost, deeper/right-altitude alternative. If the change is already at the right altitude, say so plainly.

- design: Create a design canvas - a multi-artboard visual design published as an Artifact that runs Claude Design's canvas editor (an early preview of Claude Design inside Claude Code). You DRAFT the design as .dc.html artboards laid out on one pan/zoom canvas; where saving is enabled for the user's account they refine every element visually (click-to-select, a properties panel, inline text editing, undo/redo) and Save publishes a new version for everyone, otherwise they get a view-and-export (PNG/PDF) preview of your draft. Good for UI mockups and screen flows, landing pages, marketing and social graphics, and print pieces - posters, flyers, brochures as single-page artboards; memos and reports as one flowing artboard. Use when someone wants a design, mockup, wireframe, UI or screen design, landing page, poster, flyer, brochure, banner, card, one-pager, or any visual layout they would rather tweak by hand than in code. Only for CREATING or re-seeding a canvas; an existing one is edited in its published Artifact.
- dataviz: Use this skill whenever you are about to create ANY chart, graph, plot, dashboard, or data visualization, in ANY output medium — an HTML or React artifact, inline SVG, plotting code in any library (matplotlib, plotly, d3, Recharts, …), an image/PNG you will render and upload, or a chart shared into Slack. Read it BEFORE writing the first line of chart code, choosing chart colors, building a stat tile / meter / KPI row, or laying out a dashboard. When the destination is a first-party document connector (host-designated, never self-described) that renders live charts, hand it the rows (inline, or as an uploaded data file the chart cites) rather than a rendered PNG/SVG — a picture of a chart loses hover, data inspection and per-value comments. Produces visualizations that read as one system — elegant, accessible, consistent in light and dark — using a brand-neutral placeholder palette you swap for your own. Teaches a design-system-agnostic method: a form heuristic, a color formula with a runnable validator, mark specs, and interaction rules. A validated default palette is documented in `references/palette.md` — swap that file's values for your brand's. Triggers on: "chart", "graph", "plot", "data viz", "visualization", "dashboard", "analytics", "visualize data", "categorical colors", "sequential / diverging palette", "stat tile", "sparkline", "heatmap", "legend", "axis", "tooltip", "chart colors", "color by series".
- artifact-design: Design guidance and fundamentals for Artifacts. - Load before writing any artifact, including a skill-instructed Markdown one - Markdown is never a shortcut past the design pass.
- artifact-diagramming: Diagramming know-how for Artifacts - when a picture earns its place, how to draw one that shows the real mechanism, and the inline-SVG mechanics that keep it legible in both themes.
- artifact-capabilities: Runtime capabilities a published Artifact page can be granted — behavior static HTML cannot provide on its own, such as the page reading live or connected data, remembering what people do on it (a poll, a sign-up sheet, a checklist, a document edited in place — it saves new versions of itself), keeping state shared across viewers, knowing who is viewing, asking Claude a question of its own, storing files people add, or handing the viewer a file to save. Serves this user's live capability roster and the typed call definitions. Load it whenever the user asks for an artifact needing any such runtime behavior.
- update-config: Use this skill to configure the Claude Code harness via settings.json. Automated behaviors ("from now on when X", "each time X", "whenever X", "before/after X") require hooks configured in settings.json - the harness executes these, not Claude, so memory/preferences cannot fulfill them. Also use for: permissions ("allow X", "add permission", "move permission to"), env vars ("set X=Y"), hook troubleshooting, or any changes to settings.json/settings.local.json files. Examples: "allow npm commands", "add bq permission to global settings", "move permission to user settings", "set DEBUG=true", "when claude stops show X". Pass --comment to post findings as inline PR comments, or --fix to apply the findings to the working tree after the review.
- simplify: Review the changed code for reuse, simplification, efficiency, and altitude cleanups, then apply the fixes. Quality only — it does not hunt for bugs; use /code-review for that.

Do NOT invoke for one-off tasks.
- schedule: Create, update, list, or run scheduled cloud agents (routines) that execute on a cron schedule. - When the user wants to schedule a recurring cloud agent, set up automated tasks, create a cron job for Claude Code, or manage their scheduled agents/routines. - claude-api: Reference for the Claude API / Anthropic SDK — model ids, pricing, params, streaming, tool use, MCP, agents, caching, token counting, model migration.
TRIGGER — read BEFORE opening the target file; don't skip because it "looks like a one-liner" — whenever: the prompt names Claude/Anthropic in any form (Claude, Anthropic, Fable, Opus, Sonnet, Haiku, `anthropic`, `@anthropic-ai`, `claude-*`, `us.anthropic.*`, `[1m]`); the user asks about an LLM (pricing/model choice/limits/caching) — never answer from memory; OR the task is LLM-shaped with provider unstated (agent/MCP/tool-definition/multi-agent/RAG/LLM-judge/computer-use; generate/summarize/extract/classify/rewrite/converse over NL; debugging refusals/cutoffs/streaming/tool-calls/tokens).

- run: Launch and drive this project's app to see a change working. Use when asked to run, start, or screenshot the app, or to confirm a change works in the real app (not just tests). First looks for a project skill that already covers launching the app; otherwise falls back to built-in patterns per project type (CLI, server, TUI, Electron, browser-driven, library).

func TestRepoMirrorCreate_SynchronousOptOut(t *testing.T) {
	setupTestRepo(t)
	writeSettings(t, `{"async_mirror_requests":false}`)

	var paths []string
	client := newMirrorRequestClient(t, func(w http.ResponseWriter, r *http.Request) {
		paths = append(paths, r.URL.Path)
		if r.Method != http.MethodPost || r.URL.Path != mirrorsAPIPath {
			t.Errorf("unexpected request %s %s", r.Method, r.URL.Path)
			w.WriteHeader(http.StatusNotFound)
			return
		}
		writeJSONResponse(t, w, http.StatusCreated, &coreapi.CreatedMirror{
			Created:   true,
			MirrorId:  "mirror-1",
			MirrorUrl: "entire://cluster/gh/owner/repo",
		})
	})
	previousClient := clusterCoreClient

## Verdict

The core mechanism choice is correct and at the right altitude. One genuine altitude gap remains at the call site, plus a stale doc line.

### Confirmed right-altitude (no action)

**`cmd/entire/cli/settings/settings.go:155, 1300, 1934-1936`** — the `*bool` + `mergeRawBoolPtr` + `Is…Enabled()` method trio is the codebase's existing mechanism for "default true, explicitly settable to false", not a parallel invention. `Telemetry` (:114, :1306, :1744), `SignCheckpointCommits` (:175, :1309, :1939), and `TrailsEnabled` (:214) all use it; the new accessor body is character-for-character the `IsSignCheckpointCommitsEnabled` shape.

**`cmd/entire/cli/settings/settings.go:1028`** — `settings := &EntireSettings{Enabled: true}` is not a new hardcode; `origin/main`'s `loadFromFile` has exactly this default (main line 1029, with a `// Default to enabled` trailing comment). Deleting `loadFromFileWithDefaults` restores the pre-branch shape rather than removing an established defaults mechanism, and it removes a two-loader fork that only one caller used. Only nit: main's `// Default to enabled` comment was dropped in the collapse.

**`Save` / `saveToFile` (settings.go:1954-1971)** — nothing further needed for pointer bools. `jsonutil.MarshalIndentWithNewline` over the struct gives `nil → key absent`, `&false → "async_mirror_requests": false`, which is precisely the requirement, and is how `SignCheckpointCommits` already persists. I checked whether the underlying hazard (default-true field with `omitempty`) exists elsewhere: it does not — the only plain-`bool` default-true field, `Enabled` (settings.go:87), deliberately omits `omitempty` so it always serializes. So this is a single-field fix because the field was the only instance, not because the fix is shallow.

### Finding 1 — default policy is re-derived (and inverted) at the one call site

- **File/line:** `cmd/entire/cli/repo_mirror.go:496-499`
- **Summary:** `opts.async` is left at its `false` zero value when `LoadEntireSettings` errors, so the "default true" lives half in the accessor and half in a call-site `if err == nil` branch — and the call-site half decides *false*.
- **Cost:** Any settings-load failure (no `.entire` dir per `config.go:52-55`, unreadable/invalid settings) silently routes to the synchronous path, directly contradicting the help text three lines above at `repo_mirror.go:487-489` ("uses the asynchronous request route by default"). This is the only consumer, so the field itself is otherwise fully behind the accessor (`rg` across `cmd/` and `e2e/` finds no other reads), but the default is still expressed in two places.
- **Deeper alternative:** the codebase already has the two-tier shape for exactly this — a method plus a package-level ctx form that encodes the fail-open direction. `IsSignCheckpointCommitsEnabled(ctx)` (settings.go:1945-1952) returns `true` on load error; `IsTelemetryEnabled(ctx)` returns `false`, matching its opt-in semantics. Add the matching `func IsAsyncMirrorRequestsEnabled(ctx context.Context) bool` returning `true` on error, and collapse the call site to a single line: `opts := mirrorCreateOptions{async: settings.IsAsyncMirrorRequestsEnabled(cmd.Context()), noWait: noWait, timeout: waitTimeout}`. Three lines and a swallowed error become one, and the default exists in exactly one place.

### Finding 2 — stale changelog contradicts the new default

- **File/line:** `CHANGELOG.md:16`
- **Summary:** Still documents the setting as opt-in: "Opt in with `\"async_mirror_requests\": true`; default off (#2207)".
- **Cost:** Shipped user-facing docs now state the opposite of the behavior; the flip has no changelog entry of its own.
- **Alternative:** add an entry for the default flip rather than editing the historical #2207 line.

### Finding 3 (minor) — test pins a per-field instance of a generic property

- **File/line:** `cmd/entire/cli/settings/settings_test.go:669-716`
- **Summary:** `TestSave_PreservesAsyncMirrorRequestsPresence` asserts a marshaling property (`nil` absent / explicit value preserved through LoadFromFile→Save) that holds for every optional pointer field, but is written for one key.
- **Cost:** Low. `sign_checkpoint_commits` and `telemetry` have no equivalent round-trip guard (`settings_test.go:136,192` only covers load), so the next default-true field gets no protection from this test.
- **Alternative:** if you want the guard to carry, make the table drive over `{key, json}` pairs covering `async_mirror_requests`, `sign_checkpoint_commits`, and `telemetry`. Acceptable as-is given it is guarding a requirement that was just broken.
